screening.reason: Reports a CNN-based diagnostic prediction (ASD vs. control) analysis of ABIDE I resting-state fMRI functional connectivity, including a leave-site-out evaluation (Inclusion 2, 3).

evidence_spans.text: detect ASD correctly with an accuracy of 70.22% using the ABIDE I dataset and the CC400
evidence_spans.claim: The proposed CNN detects ASD with 70.22% accuracy on ABIDE I using the CC400 atlas.

evidence_spans.text: The inclusion criteria for sites was having at least 20 subjects meeting other criteria for inclusion like successful preprocessing with manual visual inspection of normalization to MNI space of MPRAGE.
evidence_spans.claim: Site inclusion required at least 20 subjects and successful preprocessing/normalisation QC.

evidence_spans.text: There are 1,112 subjects (539 diagnosed with ASD, and 573 typical controls) in the ABIDE I dataset, reduced to 871 subjects after preprocessing.
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE I (1,112 subjects: 539 ASD/573 TD) was reduced to 871 subjects after preprocessing.

evidence_spans.text: The Preprocessed Connectomes Project (PCP) is a publicly available preprocessed version of data from both the 1,000 Functional Connectomes Project (FCP) and the International Neuroimaging Data-Sharing Initiative (INDI)3. We used data from the FCP using the conﬁgurable pipeline, the Analysis of Connectomes (CPAC).
evidence_spans.claim: Data were preprocessed via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project using CPAC.

evidence_spans.text: We used the CC400 functional parcellation atlas of the brain throughout our study.
evidence_spans.claim: The CC400 functional parcellation atlas was used throughout.

evidence_spans.text: We achieved an accuracy of 70.22 %, which is better than the rest of the reported works (Table 4).
evidence_spans.claim: The CNN achieved 70.22% 10-fold CV accuracy, better than prior reported works.

evidence_spans.text: we used a leave-site-out approach for our proposed CNN, SVM, KNN, and RF classiﬁers (Heinsfeld et al., 2018). In this method, each site is taken as one fold in the dataset, and we applied a cross-validation approach on the remaining sites instead of diﬀerent folds. Therefore, each time, one site out of 17 is used to test, and the other sites are used for training.
evidence_spans.claim: Performance was also evaluated using a leave-site-out approach across the 17 ABIDE I sites.

evidence_spans.text: DATA AVAILABILITY STATEMENT The datasets generated for this study are available on request to the corresponding author.
evidence_spans.claim: Data are available on request to the corresponding author, not openly released.

assessments.support: Cohort origin, site-inclusion rule, and the reduction from 1,112 to 871 subjects after preprocessing QC are explicit: "There are 1,112 subjects (539 diagnosed with ASD, and 573 typical controls) in the ABIDE I dataset, reduced to 871 subjects after preprocessing."
Pipeline (CPAC/PCP) and atlas (CC400) are named with preprocessing steps described.
States ADOS/ADI-R were used for ASD diagnosis or typical-control confirmation at most sites.

Uses 10-fold CV and an additional leave-site-out evaluation across all 17 sites (reduces pooled-CV site leakage), but the text does not state whether feature/hyperparameter selection was confined to training folds.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort, QC-driven sample reduction, pipeline, atlas and diagnosis source are all reported, and a leave-site-out evaluation is included alongside 10-fold CV; the main residual gap is that within-fold leakage control for hyperparameter/feature selection is not explicitly described.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (1D CNN) using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI (1,112 subjects, 539 ASD/573 TD, 17 sites), reduced to 871 subjects after CPAC preprocessing QC (a separate statement reports 505 ASD/530 TD as the dataset used).
narrative_row.methods: CPAC/PCP-preprocessed functional connectivity (CC400 atlas) fed into a 1D CNN; compared against optimised SVM, KNN and Random Forest; evaluated via 10-fold CV and a leave-site-out scheme across all 17 sites.
narrative_row.outcomes: CNN achieved 70.22% 10-fold CV accuracy, outperforming SVM (69%), KNN (62%) and RF (60%); leave-site-out accuracy varied by site, exceeding 70% at KKI, SDSU and USM.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Exact ASD/TD split of the final 871-subject analysed sample not stated; no numeric motion/FD cut-off given; data available only on request, not openly released; within-fold leakage control for hyperparameter tuning not described.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Combines a standard pooled 10-fold CV evaluation with an explicit leave-site-out analysis across all 17 ABIDE I sites, making site-level generalisation directly reportable for the dataset-publication link.

kg_link.cohort_description: ABIDE I (1,112 subjects: 539 ASD/573 TD, 17 sites; site inclusion required >=20 subjects passing successful preprocessing/MNI-normalisation QC), reduced via CPAC preprocessing to 871 analysed subjects; a separate statement in the same paper reports 505 ASD/530 typical controls as the dataset used.
kg_link.pipeline: CPAC (Configurable Pipeline for Analysis of Connectomes) via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project
kg_link.finding: CNN achieved 70.22% 10-fold CV accuracy on ABIDE I with the CC400 atlas, outperforming SVM/KNN/RF baselines; a leave-site-out evaluation across all 17 sites found accuracy above 70% at the KKI, SDSU and USM sites.
evidence_quotes: There are 1,112 subjects (539 diagnosed with ASD, and 573 typical controls) in the ABIDE I dataset, reduced to 871 subjects after preprocessing.
We achieved an accuracy of 70.22 %, which is better than the rest of the reported works (Table 4).

we used a leave-site-out approach for our proposed CNN, SVM, KNN, and RF classiﬁers (Heinsfeld et al., 2018). In this method, each site is taken as one fold in the dataset, and we applied a cross-validation approach on the remaining sites instead of diﬀerent folds. Therefore, each time, one site out of 17 is used to test, and the other sites are used for training.
